claims.text: High-temperature structural and chemical stability is governed by an interplay among nanoparticle composition, crystal structure, and defects.
The initial nanoparticles may have varying compositions and crystal structures.
Composition and crystal structure will be varied systematically as the intervention.
The relevant catalytic service-temperature range is 773–1173 K.
The relevant thermoelectric service-temperature range is 473–1923 K.
Defects and crystal structure mediate nanoparticle stability under high-temperature service.
Synthesis–structure–property relationships arising from composition, crystal structure, and defects cause improved high-temperature stability and performance.
Multi-element nanoparticles will have better high-temperature stability than single-element nanoparticles.
Multi-element nanoparticles will have better high-temperature performance than single-element nanoparticles.
Single-element nanoparticles constitute the experimental baseline.
The hypothesis is bounded by temperature, application conditions, composition, and crystal structure.
The precise interaction among composition, crystal structure, defects, stability, and performance is uncertain.
High-temperature microstructural evolution and defect dynamics will be examined using HRTEM and atom probe tomography.
